result: The first birds begin before the light. A single note, then another, tentative. The sky is a deep blue, like ink diluted. Slowly, the edges of the curtains brighten from grey to gold. The world is not awake, but it is stirring. The trees are dark shapes, holding their breath. A car passes somewhere distant, a soft hiss on wet asphalt. It smells like rain, though it has not rained yet. The air through the open window is cool and damp. On the sill, a small spider has woven a web between the potted plant and the glass. The web is beaded with tiny droplets, each one a prism for the growing light. Inside, the house is still. The clock on the wall ticks, a sound that seems too loud in the quiet. I stand at the window, watching the slow reveal of the day. There is no urgency here. The sun takes its time, pulling the shadows back, one hedgerow at a time. This is the best part of the day, before the noise begins, before the demands. A cup of coffee cools on the table, its scent mixing with the damp earth. The first bird is joined by others, a chorus building in argument. The day is here. But for one more minute, I hold on to the stillness, letting it fill the spaces between my thoughts. The web shivers. The spider is moving.
